title: Ferroelastic Fantastic: Probing Dynamically Induced Multiferroic Polarization via in-situ 4D-STEM
content: Multiferroic materials, characterized by their simultaneous ferroelectric, ferromagnetic, and ferroelastic orders, present a promising platform for next-generation technologies in memory devices, sensors, and actuators and future quantum technology. A comprehensive understanding of the interplay between these ferroic properties, particularly under dynamic conditions, is essential for unlocking their full potential. This work explores the emergent ferroelectric and ferromagnetic orders within ferroelastic systems during dynamics using advanced in-situ four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D-STEM). By combining the spatial resolution of electron microscopy with the temporal sensitivity of in-situ experiments, we probe the dynamic structural transformations driving polarization in these materials.
